verdict.line: You lose if you facetank his Q-empowered autos before level 3; you win if you poke with Q and let your item spike take over after level 7.

brief.thesis: Sett's W (Haymaker) passively banks every point of damage he takes as Grit, so standing in prolonged trades against him directly fuels the shield and true/physical damage punch he unloads later — extended exchanges feed him, they don't punish him. K'Sante's answer is range and burst windows: Q (Ntofo Strikes) pokes from 450 range and stacks toward a pulling shockwave, and W (Path Maker) takes reduced damage while charging before it stuns, so you can dictate when the fight actually starts instead of trading face to face.

tell.watch: Sett's Grit meter under his HP bar

theirWindow.when: Grit bar full after you've traded autos
theirWindow.what: His W (Haymaker) consumes all stored Grit for a shield plus true damage center/physical sides — back off and let it go to waste rather than eating it mid-trade.

yourWindow.when: W (Path Maker) off cooldown, he commits forward
yourWindow.what: Charge the reduced-damage window as he closes with Q's move speed, then dash into the stun and follow with an auto for the passive's bonus mark damage before he can Grit-shield out.

start.why: Sett lives on his alternating left/right punch autos, and the block-on-hit plus regen from Doran's Shield blunts exactly that pattern through levels 1-3 before W is up.

boots.why: Sett's entire kit — Q's empowered autos, his base punches, even his passive Pit Grit regen — runs through physical auto-attack damage, which is exactly what Steelcaps reduces.

core.why: Adds on-hit slow and attack speed that pairs with Q's stack generation, letting you threaten the 2-stack shockwave faster in trades.
The low-HP damage reduction and omnivamp directly offsets Sett's Pit Grit healing and Q burst once fights go long.
Stacking resistances scale a 1v1 duel in your favor the longer it runs, which matters since Sett wants extended exchanges.

situational.when: sett builds into attack speed or crit to maximize his double-punch autos
sett gets ahead and starts threatening a full Q into R all-in
you're losing the early all-in window before level 6 and need grievous wounds plus armor fast

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the short-trade, poke-then-reset pattern you need against Sett — it builds permanent health and punishes his autos without requiring you to stand in extended exchanges that feed his Grit.

summoners.why: Teleport resets you after short trades and gets you back before Sett can punish a missed recall, while Flash is your out against Facebreaker's pull or a Show Stopper grab; Flash+Ignite is the alternative if you're confident taking the level 1-5 all-in window yourself.

playing.title: Poke, don't facetank
playing.detail: Use Q (Ntofo Strikes) at 450 range to chip him down. Standing in auto trades banks Grit for his W shield and nuke, so short hits beat long exchanges.

playing.title: Track the wave for his E
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies sit on opposite sides of him; if the minion wave is bunched on one side, it just slows. Push or freeze the wave to one side before trading.

playing.title: Charge W into his engage
playing.detail: Path Maker takes reduced damage while charging, so pop it as he commits with Q's move speed bonus, then dash into the stun rather than trading autos first.

playing.title: Hold E for his burst window
playing.detail: Footwork's dash and shield is your out after he lands Q-empowered autos or during his R combo — don't burn it just to poke.

playing.title: Respect level 6 cooldowns
playing.detail: The Show Stopper is a 400-range grab on a 120s cooldown at rank 1. Don't overextend right as he hits 6, but don't play scared of it once it's down.

playing.title: Bank Q stacks for the pull
playing.detail: At 2 stacks, Ntofo Strikes fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in — use it to drag Sett into W's stun instead of walking up to him first.

playing.title: Save R for an empty Grit bar
playing.detail: All Out knocks him through walls and transforms your kit with more damage and healing. It's strongest when his W has already been spent and can't shield him out.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the ability interactions, trade windows, and timing calls are my own tactical read, not sourced data.
